## Why This Is Asked
Tests understanding of hazard-pointer reclamation, publication-order guarantees, and cross-CPU memory ordering under NUMA. It probes correctness in lock-free updates and safe reclamation with real-world implications.

## Key Concepts
- Hazard pointers and grace periods
- Atomic publish vs initialization order
- Release/acquire memory barriers
- NUMA visibility and cross-node ordering
- Safe reclamation trade-offs

## Code Example
```javascript
// C-like pseudo
struct Node { int data; int ready; };
Node* n = alloc();
n->data = 123;
// no barrier yet
cas(&head, old, n); // publish before initialization
```

## Trade-offs
- Release/acquire: minimal overhead but requires careful ordering
- Ready flag: simpler logic but adds extra field and check
- Full fence: strongest guarantees but highest performance cost

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests mastery of memory ordering and IPC patterns beyond high-level concepts, focusing on practical correctness under contention.

## Key Concepts
- Acquire/release semantics on per-slot sequencing
- Avoiding torn reads in shared memory IPC
- Cache coherence and memory fencing implications

## Code Example
```c
// Pseudocode sketch of per-slot slot
typedef struct { uint64_t seq; uint8_t payload[64]; } Slot;
Slot slot;
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test under high contention to detect rare races?
- What architecture-specific pitfalls might you encounter (x86 vs ARM)?
